title: Function Declaration vs Expression
Function Expression Not Hoisted
code:
console.log(greet('Alice'));

const greet = name => `Hello, ${name}`;

bugs.explanation: Function expressions (including arrow functions) assigned to `const`/`let`/`var` are not hoisted the same way as function declarations. Calling before the assignment throws `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'greet' before initialization`. Declare before use.

title: Arguments Object
Arrow Function No arguments Object

bugs.fix: const sum = (...args) => args.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
bugs.explanation: Arrow functions do not have their own `arguments` object. Accessing `arguments` inside an arrow function refers to the `arguments` of the nearest enclosing regular function (or throws `ReferenceError` at the top level). Use rest parameters `...args` instead.
